title: Determination 2023-016: Whether showers constructed without inbuilt seating or handrails comply with clause G1.3.4 of the Building Code
jurisdiction: New Zealand: Nelson City Council as building consent authority; MBIE determination under the Building Act 2004. Non-Alberta comparative record.
code_edition: NZ Building Code (Schedule 1, Building Regulations 1992). G1/AS1 Amendment 6 (issued 10 October 2011) is cited for the sanitary-fixture table (p.9 fn 13). The building consent was issued in June 2017 (p.3 §2.1).

facts.text: The internal fit-out of a wellness centre in Nelson included float rooms with a toilet, a level-threshold shower and a float pod. The showers in these rooms are the only showers available to the public.
Building consent BC170335 for the fit-out was issued in June 2017, and an amendment was issued in November 2017.
The approved plans annotated one float room shower fitted off as accessible unit. The accessibility report said one shower would be fitted with seat and grab rails.
In May 2021 the authority listed the outstanding items for a code compliance certificate, including the fixtures for the accessible bathroom.

In place of the inbuilt fold-down seat and handrail shown in the consent, the lessee proposed a removable shower seat designed for people needing support. The authority refused it in place of the fixed features.

Clause G1.3.4 reads: personal hygiene facilities provided for people with disabilities shall be accessible. The matter is determined under section 177(1)(a) and the Office for Disability Issues was consulted under section 170.
The lessee's submission: removable shower seats are found in almost every care facility and benefit clients, and the lessee disputes the outstanding requirement.
The lessee proposed, as an alternative solution, a removable shower seat that could be moved between rooms.

limitations: Regulator determination on an accessibility fixtures dispute. The lessee made no formal submission to the determination and its position is taken from correspondence.
The determination is about one wellness-centre fit-out. It is not a general ruling on movable fixtures.
The decision (p.10 §6.1) is in the same PDF as the facts. Outcome leakage is true unless redacted.
Owner and tenant names and the street address are left out of the prompt.
Applies to the New Zealand Building Code only. No Alberta applicability is asserted.
